_comment: The libgit2 wrap campaign's decomposition, as specs/decomposition.md describes, of the libgit2.so link unit the build links (crustify/builds/plain/build.ninja): one module per translation unit its link line names, with the headers carrying the TU's name and its tests, the shared headers (include/git2/types.h, common.h, cert.h, odb_backend.h, sys/odb_backend.h, sys/refdb_backend.h, sys/stream.h, deps/xdiff/xdiff.h, xtypes.h, ...) split item by item with the file entries' items lists, and a header module for each header implementing what no TU does (src/util/integer.h, array.h, bitvec.h, hashmap_str.h, staticstr.h, src/libgit2/stream.h, src/libgit2/common.h, deps/ntlmclient/utf8.h). The TUs the configured build compiles empty are configured out: src/libgit2/streams/openssl_dynamic.c, openssl_legacy.c, schannel.c, stransport.c, src/libgit2/transports/auth_gssapi.c, auth_sspi.c, ssh_exec.c and winhttp.c. Out of scope, and so owned by no module: the deprecated items (deprecated.h, cred_helpers.h, sys/cred.h and the GIT_DEPRECATE_HARD blocks of the other public headers, such as git_oid_fromstr and git_blame_get_hunk_count) and the declarations the configured build never defines (git_transport_dummy, git_blame_file_from_buffer, git_tree_cache_free, ...); the configurations under crustify/wavefront/configs/libgit2/<index>/ name them in out_of_scope.items. Every module is wrap, as the campaign is; the seven foundational ones hold the allocators, releasers and cloners of type-erased memory and of strings (src/util/alloc.c, the four src/util/allocators/, deps/reftable/basics.c and src/util/strlist.c), each foundational whole. depends_on counts edges in each module's own wavefront graph; the order cuts the foundational modules' failure-path dependencies on src/util/errors.c, and within each cycle every dependency on a member ranked later. counters.loc counts nonblank, noncomment lines of each owned entity's span: its definition in the TU or an internal header, its declaration or definition in an API header. Every path is below the C root, c/.

std.notes: no replaceable allocator hooks (reftable_set_alloc) for the C that keeps allocating through them; reftable_buf maps to Vec<u8>, binsearch to binary_search_by, the big-endian helpers to from_be_bytes/to_be_bytes

allocates by Layout rather than by size and aborts on allocation failure through handle_alloc_error, where git__malloc returns NULL and records an out-of-memory error; the replaceable git_allocator vtable installed through GIT_OPT_SET_ALLOCATOR, which C keeps calling, has a counterpart only in #[global_allocator], fixed at link time
no size-prefixed blocks, no poisoning of freed memory and no failure on zero-length allocations
GlobalAlloc takes a Layout and has no file/line arguments; the vtable shape git_allocator expects is not provided

crates.notes: parses request and response heads only, without the callback-driven body, chunked transfer-encoding and keep-alive state machine llhttp generates; no lenient-parsing flags
no settings/callback API (llhttp_settings_t), pause/resume or error-reason reporting
no keep-alive or message-needs-EOF decisions after the head

std.notes: case-insensitive comparisons and searches (utf8casecmp, utf8casestr) and utf8makevalid have no direct counterparts; ASCII-only case mapping differs from str::to_lowercase

crates.notes: an SSPI-shaped NTLM implementation: no ntlm_client_* message API, and its own credential and target-name handling
NTLMv2 message construction only; small, single-maintainer crate without the LM/NTLMv1 paths or the client state machine
MD4 only
HMAC only, with md-5 for HMAC-MD5
DES only; random bytes need a separate RNG

std.notes: String::from_utf16 rejects unpaired surrogates rather than reporting the position; no ntlm_unicode_ctx
no fixed error-code-to-string table
BinaryHeap is a max-heap over Ord; the merged-iterator ordering by record key and table index needs a custom Ord, and removal of arbitrary entries is not supported
an unbalanced binary search tree keyed by a comparison callback; BTreeMap needs Ord keys

crates.notes: tokenization and line hashing are internal to the crate; no mmfile, chastore or emit-record helpers
its interner replaces record classification, without xdiff's whitespace-ignoring hash variants

std.notes: no version-checked option structures

crates.notes: no callback-driven execution over a partial buffer
the unavoidable-bit-condition check is internal to the crate
collision detection and the safe-hash mode match; no collision callback (SHA1DCSetCallback) and no switch to disable UBC checks

std.notes: thread_local! keys are static; git_tlsdata keys are created at runtime with a destructor

crates.notes: per-object thread-local values, as git_tlsdata_* provide

std.notes: no thread-local last-error record with class codes, no saved and restored error state

crates.notes: pure Rust, with the same SHA-256 output; no OpenSSL engine selection
a common Digest trait, with sha1-checked and sha2 as its SHA-1 and SHA-256; no algorithm-tagged context or hex formatting
the same engine and semantics, but patterns are &str, so the non-UTF-8 patterns git_regexp_compile accepts cannot be compiled
a different engine: no backreferences or lookaround that PCRE2 patterns may use
Myers and histogram only, no patience, no whitespace-ignoring flags, no indent heuristic or hunk compaction; output differs in hunk placement
Myers, patience and LCS without histogram or xdiff's heuristics
unified-diff formatting without function-name context lines (find_func) or xdiff's hunk callbacks
its histogram algorithm differs in fallback and tie-breaking, so hunks can differ
three-way merge without xdiff's merge levels, favor modes, zealous conflict reduction or diff3 marker styles
patience diff without xdiff's fallback to Myers on unique-line failure

std.notes: no reference-counted init/shutdown with registered shutdown callbacks
no out-of-memory sentinel state, no base85/base64/hex/quoting helpers, no git_str_rtrim/unquote etc.

crates.notes: covers git_str_encode_base64/decode_base64 only

std.notes: git_buf is C-owned storage handed across the API; no NUL-terminated ptr/size/reserved layout

crates.notes: a global logger with levels; git_trace_set installs one callback with libgit2's own levels (fatal..trace) and a minimum level, which map onto log::Level only approximately
parses RFC 2822/3339 and strict formats; no git approxidate (relative dates, "yesterday", "noon") or git's offset formats
RFC 2822 parsing and offset arithmetic only; no approxidate
a bump arena without git_pool's fixed item size, string helpers (git_pool_strdup/strcat) or pointer-in-pool test

std.notes: git_utf8_iterate decodes one code point and reports invalid sequences as -1; str::from_utf8 validates whole buffers
strtol variants with git's overflow handling, git__strntolower, git__prefixcmp and the other string helpers map onto str methods individually

crates.notes: hex encoding and decoding only; no object-id type, shortening (git_oid_shorten) or SHA-1/SHA-256 tagging
WHATWG URLs: no scp-like git URLs (git_net_url_parse_scp), no redirect application or git's default ports and validity rules
covers the Basic credential encoding only, not the auth-context scheme
xoshiro256** itself; libgit2 seeds it from time, pid and getentropy

std.notes: no git path normalization (git_fs_path_squash_slashes, prettify), .git ownership checks or case-folding comparisons

crates.notes: home and XDG config directories; no git search-path lists (global, xdg, system, programdata, template) set through GIT_OPT_SET_SEARCH_PATH

std.notes: covers the file operations; p_* wrappers retry on EINTR and set libgit2 errors

crates.license: Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception OR Apache-2.0 OR MIT
crates.notes: safe syscalls without libgit2's error reporting

std.notes: no block-source vtable or mmap-backed reads
no recursive mkdir with base-path and permission policy, rmdir_r flags, fake-mtime handling or file-stamp tracking

crates.notes: temporary files only
atomic replace on commit; no git .lock-file protocol, streamed zlib deflate or SHA-1 hashing of the written content

std.notes: case-insensitive keying of index entries needs a custom Hash/Eq

crates.notes: parses plain unified diffs; no git extended headers (renames, modes, index lines) or binary patches

std.notes: git_pqueue optionally caps its size and keeps the smallest items, sorting with a comparison callback
covers spawn, pipes, environment and wait; no git_process_result_msg formatting

crates.notes: glob syntax close to wildmatch but not identical in "**" and bracket handling; no WM_PATHNAME/WM_CASEFOLD flags as such
only "*" and "?"; no brackets, "**" or path semantics
gitignore-style pattern matching only; no attribute assignments or macros
gitignore matching (gitignore::Gitignore) without libgit2's repository-scoped rule stack, git_ignore_add_rule or core.excludesfile lookup
glob matching without git pathspec magic or git_pathspec_match_list results
three-way text merge without xdiff's favor modes, marker sizes or diff3 style
Compress/Decompress cover deflate and inflate streams; no deflateBound for sizing output, and git_zstream_get_output's chunked loop is the caller's
applies a unified patch to text; no index/workdir targets, binary patches or git_apply_options callbacks
memory maps only; no window cache with global mapped-memory and open-file limits

std.notes: no git_stream vtable and no connect timeout policy from GIT_OPT_SET_SERVER_CONNECT_TIMEOUT applied through poll

crates.notes: SslStream over any Read + Write covers the TLS session and verification; no git_stream vtable, no git certificate-check callback contract or cipher defaults
platform TLS without custom CA-file locations per call or access to the peer X509 for git_cert_x509
an HTTP/1.1 client without git's proxy and credential-retry loop, certificate callbacks or streaming over a git_stream
HTTP machinery without a client policy for git's auth negotiation and redirects
